title: Day 10: Wheat harvest brings mixed results in western Kansas - NewsBreak
text: WICHITA, Kan. (KSNW) — Western Kansas farmers are seeing mixed results as the 2025 wheat harvest reaches its tenth day. While test weights and grain quality are generally strong, yields vary depending on location and weather conditions. In Kearny County, farmer Gary Millershaski said yields were average to above average, with decent test weights. Protein levels were a bit low, and frequent equipment breakdowns caused delays. In Colby, Eric Sperber of Cornerstone Ag said harvest is about 85% complete, but volume is down 35% to 40% from normal. Test weights are holding up, and protein levels are mostly strong. Yields are slightly below average at about 35 bushels per acre. “It has been a weird harvest,” Sperber said, pointing out that wheat ripened all at once across the state. In Norton County, farmer Chris Tanner finished harvest on July 9 after two weeks of rain delays. Early fields looked good, but others were left unharvested due to weeds and low test weights. He said dry weather nearly ruined the crop before a small rain saved it in June. Yields ranged from 20s to 70s, depending on conditions. Farmers say variety selection, soil management, and timing made a big difference this year. The Kansas Wheat Harvest Report is part of an ongoing series tracking harvest conditions across the state. It’s produced by the Kansas Wheat Commission, Kansas Association of Wheat Growers, Kansas Grain and Feed Association, and the Kansas Cooperative Council. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to KSN-TV.
